question: Does input-dependent matching outperform a strong fixed action as well as randomized matching?
data: Dense, fresh S7 and SALL at exactly 33,000,000,000 training tokens; fresh panel R=1024 records, 16 positions each
metric_unit: Comparator CE minus policy CE, micro-nat per selected event
aggregation: Pooled equal-domain readout; 2000 category-stratified paired whole-record draws
conditions: All families, both A/B transfer directions, both action sets; Dense omits SAE
scale: Linear axes; intervals unadjusted; checkpoints and source banks fixed
expected_support: Positive gain against both controls would support this frozen policy within the panel
observed: Every fixed-comparator interval is negative; every global-marginal interval is positive
rival: Predictable matching can coexist with a better pooled common action
maximum_claim: Frozen policy utility in this panel; no training, retention, semantic-specialization or architecture claim
